scope_findings.claim: Project identifies as MSCA-PF European Fellowship with host Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE), Hungary, an EU Member State institution
Fellowship duration: 24-month European Fellowship, within the 12–24 month range specified for European Postdoctoral Fellowships
Fellowship is grounded in international mobility within Europe: researcher conducts work across MATE (Hungary) and MVCRI (Bulgaria), both EU Member States
Optional non-academic sector placement with AgroVIR for 6 months, described as an additional period at the end of the project for operational transferability testing

AgroVIR non-academic placement added value: project-level benefit is described (operational transferability testing under commercial farming conditions); added value for the researcher's career development is not addressed in the concept note or project summary
scope_findings.flag_reason: CC-05 requires explicit justification of added value for both the project AND the career development of the researcher. The concept note describes project-level added value (operational transferability testing) but does not address the researcher career development benefit of the AgroVIR placement. Partial compliance with CC-05; the proposal body must explicitly address researcher career benefit to fully satisfy this constraint.

scope_findings.claim: Cross-country collaboration with MVCRI, Bulgaria for geographic model transferability testing; this collaboration may constitute a formal secondment within the European Fellowship
scope_findings.flag_reason: If the MVCRI Bulgaria collaboration constitutes a formal secondment (SR-07), its duration must not exceed 12 months (half of the 24-month European Fellowship excluding any non-academic placement period, per CC-07). The concept note and project summary do not specify the duration of researcher presence at MVCRI, Bulgaria; compliance with the CC-07 half-duration limit cannot be verified from the content provided. Duration must be specified and confirmed in the full proposal.

scope_findings.claim: Research domain: agricultural water stress prediction and irrigation management using machine learning and AI for high-value processing tomato crops, targeting early physiologically grounded detection of developing crop water stress

This claim cannot be confirmed as in-scope from Tier 2B scope_requirements.json data alone.
